what_it_does: Neural Architecture Search (NAS) is the process of automatically finding the best neural network design for a task. Hardware-aware NAS must also consider the target device (like a specific GPU), so designers use surrogate models—fast mathematical models that predict how well a given network will perform on that hardware without actually running it. Building accurate surrogate models is challenging and poorly understood. This paper provides a systematic study of different surrogate model types and their strengths/weaknesses when predicting GPU performance. It analyzes factors that influence prediction accuracy across the entire pipeline: how training data is generated, which model architecture to use, how to train it, and how to optimize cost versus accuracy. The result is ESM, a framework that enables reliable surrogate model building for hardware-aware NAS.
